Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Our security team wants a concrete runbook we can hand to networking for production onboarding. Two immediate asks: 1) can you provide the specific source IP addresses or ranges we must allow for the private endpoint control plane and model egress (including any fallback pools), and 2) what TLS/SNI behavior should we expect if we terminate TLS at our edge (we have inline TLS inspection in place)?

Also: we have strict rules that all outbound traffic must be NATed via a customer-managed egress proxy; is Redwood compatible with that pattern (i.e., can you pin IPs to a proxy or do you require direct outbound sockets from the private endpoint)?

If possible, attach your runbook draft and any IP matrices. We need to schedule a final sign-off this week to keep the migration on track.

Hi Anita —

Appreciate the clear asks. Attached is our internal-runbook draft tailored to Acme (redwood-egress-operator-runbook-v0.3.pdf) and a companion IP matrix (acme-proxy-ip-matrix.xlsx). High-level answers up-front: 

- Source IPs: We publish two pools: a stable control-plane pool (3 IPv4 /27 blocks) used for management and telemetry, and a model-egress pool (ephemeral but can be restricted to a predictable NAT set if you use our egress gateway). Exact CIDRs are in the attached matrix; for now, use the three control-plane CIDRs: 34.203.112.0/27, 34.203.112.32/27, 34.203.112.64/27. Model egress IPs are normally ephemeral; if you require fixed IPs we recommend routing through a customer-managed NAT or our dedicated egress gateway (details below).

- Proxy / NAT compatibility: We support both patterns: 1) customer-managed egress proxy (recommended for maximum control) — in that case the private endpoint initiates outbound to your proxy and the proxy performs NAT with static source IPs you control; 2) Redwood-managed egress gateway — we can reserve a small set of static IPs and accept traffic through those (we require an SLA addendum for dedicated IP reservation).

- TLS/SNI and inspection: Redwood uses SNI and TLS 1.2+/1.3 for all outbound model requests. If you terminate TLS at your edge, be aware of two behaviors: a) when the proxy performs TLS inspection (MITM), we will see a proxied TLS session — this is compatible but breaks end-to-end client certificate pinning; b) if you allow TCP passthrough for SNI-only inspection, ensure SNI passthrough is preserved. Our runtime sets the Host header to the model endpoint hostname; if your inspection alters SNI or Host, requests may fail validation.

- Recommended firewall rules (minimum):
  * Allow outbound TCP 443 to our control-plane CIDRs (see matrix)
  * Allow outbound TCP 443 to 52.10.0.0/16 and 34.203.0.0/16 (model object storage & artifacts)
  * Allow outbound UDP/53 to your DNS resolvers (no direct DNS to external)
  * Deny inbound flows — all connections are originated by the private endpoint

- Observability & audit: We send tokenized telemetry over TLS to the control plane. If you require audit logs to be forwarded to your SIEM, point a collector at our metrics exporter endpoint (see Drive link).

Next steps: please review the attached matrix and confirm whether you want customer-managed NAT (we'll provide a sample iptables policy) or Redwood-managed static IP reservation (we'll need your billing signoff for the SLA addendum).

I'll be on a call tomorrow with Engineering; looping in Jonas and Rishi for IP-rotation and SLA details.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Anita — quick clarification from infra side:

On IP rotation: our model-egress pool rotates on a weekly cadence by default (automated rotation to mitigate long-lived IP churn for customers who do not pin IPs). If you choose customer-managed NAT, you will see stable source IPs (your NAT IPs) even when ours rotate. If you opt for Redwood-managed reservation, we can provide a guaranteed set and a two-week rotation window for maintenance (not weekly).

On port/host allowlisting: the runbook includes a minimal trusted-hosts file for your outbound proxy to reduce false positives; please let us know if your proxy enforces client certs — we can generate a per-customer client cert for mutual TLS to the egress gateway.

-Jonas
Director, Inference Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

1) Can you provide a single CSV with the final CIDRs and a preferred order (control plane first, then artifacts, then egress gateway)? We'll ingest into our firewall tooling.
2) For the Redwood-managed reservation option: confirm the number of public IPv4 addresses you need from us to reserve (we prefer to own the NAT IPs at our perimeter).
3) If our proxy must perform TLS interception (we have a corporate policy to do so), will Redwood flag any payloads as altered or drop them?

Also: if we sign the SLA addendum, can we get a 30-day rollback window after go-live where traffic will fail-open to Redwood-hosted fallback to avoid immediate downtime if our NAT has a configuration error?

If you can send the CSV and a short acceptance checklist, we can schedule a Friday sign-off.

Anita — thanks, yes. Deliverables attached and proposed immediate next steps below.

Deliverables included: 
- acme-proxy-ip-matrix.xlsx (CSV export included in workbook) — contains ordered CIDRs and intended use column (control-plane, artifacts, egress-gateway).
- redwood-egress-operator-runbook-v0.3.pdf — updated to include client-cert mTLS instructions and iptables sample for customer-managed NAT.
- redwood-sla-egress-addendum.docx — draft SLA addendum for dedicated IP reservation.

Acceptances & fallback: 
1) We will provide a 30-day rollback window post-go-live where traffic will automatically fall back to Redwood-hosted endpoints for the small subset of calls we mark as "critical" in the runbook (this requires the SLA addendum to be signed and a small burst reserve capacity configured).
2) If your proxy performs TLS interception, we will not intentionally drop requests — but any modification to SNI/Host or to request payloads that affect signature headers will cause request validation failures. Our recommendation is to configure the proxy to preserve SNI and Host headers and use the per-customer mTLS option for authenticity.
3) For Redwood-managed reservation where Acme prefers Redwood to advertise stable public IPs, we request you provide 2 public IPv4s to NAT from your edge for BGP-translated peers; otherwise we will assign 4 small reserved addresses on our side (billing applies).

Next steps (this week):
- You: confirm NAT ownership preference (customer-owned NAT IPs vs Redwood-managed reservation) and sign the SLA addendum if opting for Redwood-managed IPs.
- Us: export the CSV of CIDRs (attached) and schedule a 1-hour cutover dry run with your network team.

DocuSign link for SLA addendum: https://docusign.redwood.com/r/ACME-2027-EGRESS (link valid 7 days)

If you'd like, Laura and Rishi will join the cutover call to review the dry-run checklist.

Best regards,
